hints: Compare the wall thickness and the % elastic tissue for P and Q. Which one has the thicker wall (2 mm vs 1 mm) and the most elastic tissue (40%) to stretch with each pulse?

Remember arteries need thick, elastic walls for high pressure, veins need thinner walls with more collagen, and a capillary is only about 0.007 mm wide with a wall one cell thick. Can R with a 4 mm diameter and 1 mm wall be a capillary?
walkthrough:
**Spot the artery features in P**

Look first at size and wall. P has the largest diameter ($25$ mm) and the thickest wall ($2$ mm). It also has the highest % elastic tissue at 40%.

That is classic artery structure. Elastic tissue stretches and recoils to smooth out high pressure pulses from the heart.

**Spot the vein features in Q**

Now compare Q. It has a wide diameter ($20$ mm) but only half the wall thickness of P ($1$ mm). Its collagen is highest at 40% and elastic is lower at 25%.

That fits a vein. Veins carry blood at low pressure, so walls are thinner, the lumen is wide, and collagen helps prevent over-stretching.

**Check why R cannot be a capillary**

R looks smaller ($4$ mm diameter) but its wall is still $1$ mm thick with lots of muscle (35%) and elastic tissue (30%). A true capillary is microscopic, about $0.007$ mm across, with a wall only one endothelial cell thick for diffusion.

So R is far too big and too thick-walled to be a capillary. It is a smaller muscular artery (an arteriole-sized artery). That gives P = artery, Q = vein, R = artery.

options.A: Correct. P has thick wall and most elastic tissue for an artery, Q has thin wall and most collagen for a vein, and R is too large and thick-walled to be a capillary so is also an artery.
options.B: Not quite. P as artery and Q as vein is right, but R cannot be a capillary because its diameter is 4 mm and wall is 1 mm thick, much larger than a real capillary.
options.C: Swapped around. P has the thicker, more elastic wall so it is the artery, not the vein, and R is far too big to be a capillary.
options.D: Swapped around. Q has the thinner wall with high collagen so it is the vein, not the artery, and R with thick muscle and elastic wall is an artery, not a vein.
